answer: In a simple (single-predictor) logistic regression of camrelizumab treatment response on age — response coded 1 = PR (responders, n=41) vs 0 = SD/PD (non-responders, n=39), age in continuous whole years, on the 80 valid camrelizumab-treated patients — the coefficient estimate for age (change in log-odds of response per 1-year increase in age) is −0.075 (b_age = −0.07495, SE = 0.02435, z = −3.08, p = 0.0021; 95% CI −0.1227 to −0.0272). Equivalently the odds ratio per year is exp(−0.075) ≈ 0.93 (95% CI 0.88–0.97). Interpretation: each additional year of age is associated with an ~0.075 decrease in the log-odds of camrelizumab treatment response (responders were younger on average: 54.9 vs 62.4 years).
